title: Observed Galaxy Abundances at z > 6 Exceed Halo-Limited Predictions in COSMOS-Web
description: Using the COSMOS2025 JWST COSMOS-Web catalog, this paper measures the abundance of massive galaxies (log M*/Msun > 9) at z > 5 and compares them to both forward-modeled expectations and the absolute upper limit implied by the halo mass function assuming ε = 1 baryon-to-star conversion. The authors find that at z > 8, observed galaxy counts exceed even the halo-limited cap by factors of 3–10, with the tension increasing with redshift and remaining robust to extreme assumptions about contamination, mass systematics, and cosmic variance.

star_formation_efficiency.description: Definition of the baryon-to-star conversion efficiency, where M_* is stellar mass, M_h is halo mass, and f_b is the cosmic baryon fraction; ε = 1 sets the maximal (halo-limited) case used to define an absolute upper bound.

halo_limited_cap.latex: n_{\rm gal}(>M_*, z) \;\le\; n_{\rm halo}(>M_h, z)\quad\text{for}\quad M_* = f_b \, M_h
halo_limited_cap.description: Cumulative number density of galaxies cannot exceed the cumulative halo abundance when assuming 100% conversion of baryons into stars (ε = 1); used as the absolute ceiling for observed galaxy counts.

key_results.main_finding: At z > 8, observed galaxy abundances (log M*/Msun > 9) in COSMOS-Web exceed the ε = 1 halo-limited cap by factors of 3–10, with the discrepancy strengthening toward higher redshift and remaining under extreme robustness tests.

kill_criteria: KC1: Secure spectroscopy for a representative (>=70%) subsample of z > 8 candidates shows that interlopers reduce the number density of log M*/Msun > 9 galaxies by >=3x such that counts fall below the epsilon=1 halo cap across all relevant masses.

KC2: Re-analysis with alternative SPS models (including nebular emission, dust laws, and IMFs) reduces inferred stellar masses at z > 8 by >=0.5 dex, bringing cumulative abundances under the halo-limited ceiling.

KC3: Updated completeness, selection, and Eddington-bias corrections from end-to-end forward modeling decrease the z > 8 number densities by factors of 3–10, fully reconciling measurements with the halo-limit.

KC4: Independent wide-area JWST fields (e.g., PRIMER, JADES, CEERS) fail to reproduce the reported excess; a combined, cosmic-variance-weighted meta-analysis yields abundances consistent with the halo cap at z > 8.

KC5: Revised high-z halo mass functions or cosmological parameters (e.g., from CMB/lensing) increase the halo-limited abundance cap by >=10x at z > 8, eliminating the need for epsilon > 1 to match observed counts.
abstract_short: 8,447 massive galaxies (log M*/Msun > 9) at z > 5 from COSMOS-Web exceed ΛCDM halo-limited predictions.
